question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f={3}^{u},\,u=2{x}^{2}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}={3}^{u}\ln(3),\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={3}^{u}\ln(3)\cdot (4x) \\  & =4x\cdot {3}^{u}\ln(3) \\  & =4x\cdot {3}^{2{x}^{2}}\ln(3).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y={4}^{7x}$ at the point where $x=\frac{1}{7}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={4}^{u},\,u=7x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={4}^{u}\ln4,\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=7.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={4}^{u}\ln4\cdot 7 \\  & =7\ln4\cdot {4}^{u} \\  & =7\ln4\cdot {4}^{7x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=\frac{1}{7}$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=1/7} & =7\ln(4)\cdot {4}^{7(1/7)} \\  & =7\ln(4)\cdot 4 \\  & =28\ln(4)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $x=\frac{1}{7}$ is $28\ln(4).$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve $y={4}^{-7x}$ at the point where $x=\frac{1}{7}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={4}^{u},\,u=-7x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}={4}^{u}\ln(4),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-7.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={4}^{u}\ln(4)\cdot (-7) \\ & =(-7)\cdot {4}^{u}\ln(4) \\ & =-7\cdot {4}^{-7x}\ln(4).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=\frac{1}{7}$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\big|_{x=\frac{1}{7}} & =(-7)\cdot {4}^{-7(\frac{1}{7})}\ln(4) \\ & =-7\cdot {4}^{-1}\ln(4) \\ & =- \frac{7 \ln{\left(4 \right)}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $x=\frac{1}{7}$ is $- \frac{7 \ln{\left(4 \right)}}{4}.$
